questions.stem: How many strings of length 5 can be formed from an alphabet of 6 symbols if repetition is allowed?

options.misconception: Wrong belief "forbids repetition without justification" gives 720, not 7776.
Wrong belief "swaps the string length and alphabet size" gives 15625, not 7776.
Wrong belief "omits one valid string" gives 7775, not 7776.

questions.explanation: Each of the 5 positions can be filled independently by any of the 6 symbols, so by the product rule there are 6 to the power 5, namely 7776, strings.
questions.hint: Every position has the same number of independent choices.

questions.stem: In a counting model with 4 and 3, how many sequences of length 4 can be formed from an alphabet of 3 symbols if repetition is allowed?
questions.explanation: Each of the 4 positions can be filled independently by any of the 3 symbols, so by the product rule there are 3 to the power 4, namely 81, strings. The required result is 81.
questions.hint: Every position has the same number of independent choices.

questions.subject: MATH
questions.topic: Counting principles: sum and product rules
questions.learningObjective: Solve problems involving counting principles: sum and product rules.
questions.stem: A menu has 12 appetizer choices and 3 main-course choices. How many distinct two-course meals are possible?
questions.explanation: Choosing an appetizer and a main course are independent decisions, so the product rule gives 12 times 3 equals 36 distinct meals. The required result is 36.
questions.hint: Multiply the counts for independent choices.
